one_line: A craftable/deconstructable hanging structure you can buckle a human into to slowly strangle them (or yourself) to death while they dangle and struggle.
player_facing_mechanics: Buckle a human into the noose (15 seconds do_after; only 2 seconds if the target is dead or you are noosing yourself)
Monkeys get a different higher hang offset; golems and moths are rejected with a notice that their head doesn't fit
Targets without a head, or not on the noose's turf, cannot be noosed
While hung, the victim takes 5 oxyloss per processing tick and periodically gasps or shows grim struggle messages
The hung victim, the noose, and its neck overlay sway back and forth with animated pixel offsets
Bystanders take 100 ticks to untie the noose over a victim; the victim can struggle free in 150 ticks
If the victim loses gravity or loses their head, everyone is automatically unbuckled
On release the victim drops, is knocked down for 60 ticks, and their pixel/layer offsets reset
Deconstruct with a wirecutter (secondary act) to recover a cable coil
tg_systems_used: buckle system (can_buckle, buckle_mob, user_buckle_mob, post_buckle_mob, post_unbuckle_mob)
logic_parts: user_buckle_mob eligibility checks and variable do_after duration
user_unbuckle_mob differing timers for self vs bystander
post_buckle_mob / post_unbuckle_mob visual re-offset, layer swap, dropdown and knockdown
process() breathing damage, gravity/head checks, sway animation, grim messages
create_noose_overlay / move_overlay overlay lifecycle tied to movement signal and destruction
byond_specific: animate() with ELASTIC_EASING for sway and hang drop
port_notes: SS14 would model the noose as an entity with a Buckleable/Strap component plus a dedicated NooseSystem that owns the hanging state machine: a DoAfter to insert/remove, a periodic Thirst-like system tick applying Asphyxiation/oxygen damage, and a visual overlay entity tracked to the noose's transform. Movement/sway maps to sprite offset animation or a client-side sway; the movement signal maps to a Transform/component event and the gravity/head-loss auto-release maps to reactive subscriptions on those components. Destroy/deconstruct cleanup maps to a system that deletes the overlay and unregisters subscriptions, and the cable-coil drop becomes a SpawnEntityOnInteract/deconstruct result. A human must decide whether to reuse upstream SS14's choking/noose content instead of porting this fork variant, and how to represent pixel-level sway and the monkey/golem/moth exceptions in an ECS without smuggling hardcoded species data into the system.
